---
title: "cloud infrastructure & scaling"
---

## what infrastructure supplies

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| component | definition | ml use case |
|---|---|---|
| compute | processors and memory used to run programs | train models or serve predictions |
| virtual machine | a software-defined computer with its own operating environment | host an inference service |
| gpu | a graphics processing unit, suited to highly parallel computation | accelerate suitable training or inference workloads |
| object storage | storage accessed as named objects through an interface | retain datasets, model artifacts, and reports |
| networking | connections and routing between systems | carry prediction requests and access inputs |
| load balancer | a component distributing requests across service instances | spread traffic across replicas |

:::

- choose resources from measured workload needs, including model memory, data access, and response time
- a managed endpoint is a provider-operated prediction service; use one when its operations and scaling features fit the workload

## tools and scaling terms

- infrastructure as code describes desired resources in versioned configuration; use it to review and repeat environment changes
- terraform is an infrastructure-as-code tool that plans and applies resource changes through provider plugins, which connect it to a platform’s api [terraform introduction](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/intro)
- docker compose defines and runs services on an existing docker host; use it for a small local environment [compose model](https://docs.docker.com/compose/intro/compose-application-model/)
- kubernetes coordinates containerised workloads across machines; a pod runs one or more related containers, while a deployment manages replicated pods and updates [deployment concepts](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/)
- vertical scaling increases resources for one instance; horizontal scaling adds instances, or replicas
- autoscaling adjusts replica counts or resources using configured signals; kubernetes’ horizontal pod autoscaler can adjust replica counts from observed metrics [autoscaling guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/autoscaling/horizontal-pod-autoscale/)

## a local service configuration

- [download the deployment exercise](../../examples/deployment-demo.zip), which includes the earlier synthetic model and serving code
- prepare the model and image following the [packaging notes](../packaging-serving/containers.qmd), then use this `compose.yaml`

```yaml
services:
  api:
    image: ${DEMO_IMAGE:-mlops-demo:local}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${DEMO_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    cpus: 1.0
    mem_limit: 512m
    restart: "on-failure:3"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/health', timeout=2)"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s
```

- `DEMO_IMAGE` and `DEMO_PORT` are environment variables selecting the image and host port, with defaults after `:-`
- cpu and memory limits bound the container’s resources; these are example settings to measure and tune [resource limits](https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/resource_constraints/)
- a health check periodically tests service state; this one checks the readiness endpoint after startup
- `on-failure:3` allows bounded restarts after unsuccessful process exits; an unhealthy check alone does not trigger this restart policy [restart behaviour](https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/start-containers-automatically/)

```bash
docker compose config --quiet
docker compose up -d --wait
docker compose ps
```

- `config` validates the configuration; `up --wait` waits for services to run or become healthy where checks exist [compose up](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/up/)
- one local container still depends on one host; replicas need independent failure capacity and suitable request routing
- each worker process may load its own model copy, so budget memory as well as cpu before adding workers [fastapi deployment concepts](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/deployment/concepts/)
